The path of a folder of the project

Source: R/folders.R
folder.Rd

folder() gives the path of one folder of folders of initialize_project(). Project code reads each folder outside the project through it.

Usage

folder(name = "main", ...)

Arguments

name

The name of the folder in folders of initialize_project(). The default "main" is also the name of one folder given without a name.

...

Parts of a path inside the folder, each one string, for example pbn::folder("main", "sub", "d.csv"). folder() joins them to the folder with /. A part MUST NOT start with /, \\ or a drive such as C:. It MUST NOT hold .., so a path never leaves the folder.

Value

The path of the folder, or of the path inside it, one string. A folder that existed at initialize_project() has its normalised path with /, and another folder has the path as folders gave it.

Details

folder() stops before initialize_project(), and on a name that the project does not declare. The error names the declared folders. A folder that does not exist still has its path, so the code of a fake scenario runs on a computer without the real data.

run_plan() gives the folders to each worker, so folder() works in a data function and in an analysis on a worker too.

The path of a folder is never in a results file or in a cache key. The manifest names the files of a folder <folder name>/<path in the folder>, so the same data in another place gives the same results.

See also

vignette("pbn"), which builds and runs a small fake project.

Other project setup: create_project(), end_unless_real(), initialize_project(), new_version(), scenarios()

Examples

home <- file.path(tempdir(), "pbn_folder_example")
dir.create(file.path(home, "v01_functions"), recursive = TRUE)
writeLines("extends: house_2026_11_19", file.path(home, "pbn.yml"))
writeLines("CFG <- list()", file.path(home, "v01_functions", "_cfg.R"))
pbn::initialize_project(
  "v01",
  home,
  folders = c(main = file.path(home, "data"), lookup = file.path(home, "codes")),
  env = new.env()
)
#> You are NOT sourcing into .GlobalEnv. All functions will be sourced into an environment that is returned from this function.
#> Sourcing all code inside /tmp/Rtmp28uSBm/pbn_folder_example/v01_functions into 
pbn::folder("lookup")
#> [1] "/tmp/Rtmp28uSBm/pbn_folder_example/codes"
pbn::folder("main", "sub", "d.csv")
#> [1] "/tmp/Rtmp28uSBm/pbn_folder_example/data/sub/d.csv"

unlink(home, recursive = TRUE)
